English: Open Table
A humble wooden table set in the open, where nomads gather to barter simple goods or news. Marks the first step toward an organized market.
Barter Patch
A cleared patch of ground with makeshift stalls and rugs, where traders and herders meet to exchange goods, livestock, and stories.
Traders Tent
A large, sturdy tent for merchants, offering limited shelter for goods and negotiation. An essential meeting spot for traveling traders.
Merchants Pavilion
A large, colorful pavilion with dedicated spaces for goods, guards, and private deals. The centerpiece of a growing nomadic market.
Market Stand
Wooden stands and awnings form a semi-permanent market, attracting more merchants and allowing for greater scale of trade.
Exchange Room
A sturdy wooden hall with private rooms for weighing, counting, and exchanging valuables. Guards and scribes ensure fair trades.
Market Hall
A prominent timber-and-clay hall, bustling with merchants from across the steppe and beyond. A hub of commerce and negotiation.
Guild Pavilion
A vast, canvas-covered complex, where merchant guilds gather, regulate trade, and train apprentices. A sign of wealth and sophistication.
Grand Market Room
A lavish, multi-chambered market structure of timber and stone, hosting foreign envoys, caravans, and steppe nobility. Commerce flourishes at all hours.
Indian Grand Market
A magnificent domed market, inspired by the riches of the Indian subcontinent. Silk, spices, and gems flow through its halls, attracting merchants from every corner of the world.
